findings.title: Fresh installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
findings.body: When no Integration row exists yet, this branch advances the pipeline and creates/attaches the integration without checking `github_authenticated_user` against an installer identity. GitHub's installation webhook, which supplies `metadata.sender`, is asynchronous and can arrive after the setup callback (the normal test flow itself succeeds without a webhook). Consequently, a caller who can submit a newly created installation ID before its webhook is processed can associate it with their Sentry organization after authorizing any GitHub account, defeating the new installer/user validation. The flow must wait for or otherwise obtain and validate the installation sender before allowing this branch to create the organization integration.

findings.title: OAuth token and user-info request failures escape as server errors
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is executed outside the try/except, and `get_user_info` is also unguarded. A cancelled OAuth authorization callback has a valid `state` but no `code`, and a rejected/reused code can make GitHub return a non-success response; the token request can therefore raise before the code reaches the `access_token` check. Likewise, a failed `/user` request can raise. These expected failure paths produce a 500 instead of the installation failure response promised by this flow. Catch transport/API errors around both calls and return `error(...)`.

findings.title: Existing sender-less integrations crash during reinstallation
findings.body: This directly indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but `build_integration` creates metadata without `sender` unless some separate state source populated it; the regular setup test explicitly produces such metadata. If its OrganizationIntegration is later removed while the active Integration remains (for example, cleanup of the organization integration or a missed webhook), this is exactly the existing-integration/no-OrganizationIntegration path and it raises KeyError rather than returning the failure page. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as an unverifiable installation request (or obtain the sender before proceeding).
